```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>",
                      eval = torch::torch_is_installed())
```

graphlearnR is a framework for machine learning on graphs written in R on top
of the [torch](https://torch.mlverse.org) package. Nothing in it calls Python.
This article walks through one complete workflow: load a graph, split it,
train a graph neural network, evaluate it, and predict. Later articles cover
each step in depth.

```{r setup}
library(graphlearnR)
library(torch)
```

LibTorch must be installed once with `torch::install_torch()`. Every code
chunk in these articles runs only when it is available.

## A first graph

Zachary's karate club is a social network of 34 club members. The club split
into two factions, which is the node label. `dataset_karate()` returns it as a
`graph_data` object with one hot node identity features.

```{r}
g <- dataset_karate()
g
summary(g)
```

The graph is undirected. graphlearnR stores each undirected pair in both
directions, so message passing sees both, and records which stored edges
belong to the same pair in `g$edge_pair`. Node indices are 1-based
everywhere, like the rest of R.

```{r}
g$edge_index[, 1:6]
g$edge_pair[1:6]
```

## Split the nodes

`split_nodes()` adds disjoint logical masks. With a factor label it
stratifies by class, so each split keeps the class balance.

```{r}
g <- split_nodes(g, train = 0.5, val = 0.25, test = 0.25, seed = 42)
table(train = g$train_mask, label = g$y)
```

## Build and train a model

`gnn_model()` builds a stack of message passing layers. Here a two layer
GraphSAGE network maps the 34 input features to 16 hidden units and then to
two class scores.

```{r}
torch_manual_seed(1)
model <- gnn_model("sage", input_dim = 34, hidden_dim = 16, output_dim = 2,
                   dropout = 0.3)
model
```

`train_graph_model()` runs the training loop. The loss for node
classification is cross entropy on the training nodes only; the validation
nodes drive early stopping, and the best weights are restored at the end.

```{r}
fit <- train_graph_model(model, g, task = "node_classification",
                         epochs = 150, lr = 0.01, weight_decay = 5e-4,
                         early_stopping = 20, seed = 1)
fit
tail(fit$history)
```

## Evaluate and predict

`evaluate_graph_model()` scores the held out test nodes.

```{r}
evaluate_graph_model(fit, g)
```

`predict()` returns a data frame with one row per node, a predicted class,
and a probability per class. Other types return only the classes, the
probability matrix, the raw scores, or the node embeddings.

```{r}
pred <- predict(fit, g)
head(pred)
emb <- predict(fit, g, type = "embedding")
dim(emb)
```
